19.10.2023
1.

This is the first bail application filed under Section 438 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for the grant of anticipatory bail to the applicant who is apprehending his arrest in connection with Crime No.193 of 2023, registered at Police Station - Telibandha, District - Raipur, Chhattisgarh for the offence punishable under Sections 420, 467, 468, 471 and 120B of the Indian Penal Code.

entities.text: Police Station - Telibandha, District - Raipur, Chhattisgarh
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 2. The facts of the present case are that an FIR was lodged by Sameer Turak on 22.03.2023 making the allegation that the present applicant was employed in the company of Arshi Infrastructure from 02.08.2019 to 09.04.2021 and during that period he downloaded the license of the petitioner and used it in getting the work orders from various government departments.
On such a complaint, the police registered the offences as stated above against the present applicant and one Haider Ali.
3. Learned counsel appearing for the applicant would submit that the FIR was lodged against the petitioner on suspicion only.

She would further submit that earlier on similar allegations an FIR was registered bearing FIR No. 221 of 2022 lodged by the Executive Engineer of the Public Health Engineering Department, Kondagaon on 08.06.2022.
She would also submit that Haidar Ali has been enlarged on regular bail by this Court.

It is further argued by counsel for the applicant that earlier an FIR was lodged on the ground that the present applicant forged an experience certificate Jai Prakash Narayan Singh vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 19 October, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46504217/
1 and got work orders from various departments whereas, in the present FIR similar allegations have been made by the complainant that the applicant misused the license and got work orders from various departments.

entities.text: Jai Prakash Narayan Singh vs State Of Chhattisgarh
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
She would further contend that in the judgment passed by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Tarak Dash Mukharjee & Ors. vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Ors.,
reported in 2022 LiveLaw (SC) 731, it is held that the applicant cannot be prosecuted twice for a similar offence.

entities.text: Tarak Dash Mukharjee & Ors. vs. State of Uttar Pradesh and Ors
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
She would also contend that the license was issued by the Ceinsys Company on 21.04.2021 according to FIR whereas; the applicant had left the services of the complainant company on 09.04.2021.
4.
On the other hand, learned counsel for the State as well as learned counsel for the complainant would oppose the bail application.

Learned counsel for the complainant would submit that the company who had issued the license in favour of Arshi Infrastructure has given a certificate to the effect that the present applicant has misused the license which was issued to the Arshi Company.
He would further submit that the applicant has caused a loss to the company namely Arshi Infrastructure to the tune of Rs.13,00,000/- and the company who had issued the license.

He has referred to Annexure-A/7 issued by Ceinsys Company dated 28.02.2023 wherein it is clearly stated that the software license attached in your letter against the name of "M/s. OFA Consultancy Services Private Limited is the fabricated copy of the original license issued to M/s. Arshi Infrastructure Engineering Services Private Limited".

entities.text: Arshi Infrastructure Engineering Services Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: Learned State counsel would submit that the source of the FIR and the allegations in both the FIRs are entirely different.

He would further submit that an earlier FIR was registered by the Executive Engineer, Public Health Department, Kondagaon making the allegation that the present applicant forged an experience certificate and participated in the tender process and got various work orders.
On such a complaint, the police have registered the FIR against the present applicant.

He would submit that the present FIR i.e. Crime No. 193 of 2023 has been lodged by Sameer Turak making allegation that the present applicant was an employee of Arshi Infrastructure Private Limited from 02.08.2019 to 09.04.2021 and during that period he cloned the license issued by Ceinsys Tech Limited.
5. Heard learned counsel for the parties, considered their rival submissions and perused the case-diary.

6. From a perusal of the documents, it appears that the allegations made against the applicant in FIR No. 221 of 2022 and FIR No.193 of 2023 are entirely different therefore, the law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the matter of Tarak Dash Mukharjee (supra) would not apply in the present case.

It is not in dispute that the present applicant is the Proprietor of M/s. OFA Consultancy Services Private Limited and the original license which was issued to M/s. Arshi Infrastructure Engineering Services Private Limited was being misused by the present applicant.

entities.text: Arshi Infrastructure Engineering Services Private Limited
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
Further, taking into consideration the allegations made against the present applicant that he cloned the license issued by Ceinsys Company and used it for getting work orders from various departments, the application deserves to be and is hereby dismissed.
7.
Accordingly, the anticipatory bail application preferred by the applicant is dismissed.
